issues.title: Cross-field validation uses field validator
issues.description: The rule requires cross-field validation to use @model_validator decorator, but the code uses @field_validator which accesses unvalidated fields via info.data, causing order-dependent validation issues
issues.rule_name: Pydantic Models Must Use model_validator for Cross-Field Validation

issues.title: Incorrect automation_triggered_event_id for state-specific actions
issues.description: When actions_on_trigger or actions_on_resolve are executed, they should be linked to their specific triggered_event.id or resolved_event.id respectively. However, the code incorrectly uses primary_state_change_event_id (which always prefers Triggered over Resolved) for both types of actions. This breaks the tracing chain for actions_on_resolve - they will reference the wrong event ID when only a Resolved state change occurs, making it impossible to correctly trace the action back to the automation.resolved event that actually prompted it.

issues.title: Missing related resources in action.triggered event on failure path
issues.description: In the fail() method, the code builds related_resources list that includes both automation-triggered-event and triggering-event references. However, when emitting the 'prefect.automation.action.triggered' event, it incorrectly uses self._resulting_related_resources instead of the newly built related_resources list. This means the action.triggered event will not include the automation-triggered-event or triggering-event links on the failure path, breaking the traceability chain documented in the PR. Users won't be able to trace from failed actions back to their source events.

issues.title: Validation incorrectly rejects proactive triggers with automation_triggered_event_id
issues.description: The field_validator for automation_triggered_event_id prevents setting this field when triggering_event is None. However, proactive triggers (which have no triggering_event) still create automation.triggered events and need to link actions to them via automation_triggered_event_id. The code in triggers.py sets automation_triggered_event_id=primary_state_change_event_id for all actions including proactive triggers, causing Pydantic validation to fail at runtime. This breaks all proactive automations, which is a critical functional regression.

pr.title: Link automation.action.* events to automation.triggered event

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds an `automation_triggered_event_id` to `TriggeredAction`, populates it in `triggers.act()` with the ID of the `automation.triggered` / `automation.resolved` state-change event, and turns it into an `automation-triggered-event` related resource on `prefect.automation.action.*` events. It also adds a `triggering-event` related resource to the `executed` event (previously only on `failed`) and makes the action event emission in `actions.py` consistent across the `succeed` and `fail` paths. The docs and the test updates across the action modules are consistent with that intent.

The core idea is sound, but the implementation has a blocking bug. The new `field_validator` on `TriggeredAction` rejects any `automation_triggered_event_id` when `triggering_event` is None. `act()` always sets that ID whenever a Triggered or Resolved state change exists, and proactive triggers have no triggering event, so `act()` now raises a ValidationError and no actions are published for proactive automations. The `fail()` path also has its two related-resource lists swapped relative to the base commit, so `action.triggered` on failure loses its `triggering-event` link and never gets the new `automation-triggered-event` link. That contradicts the PR's own test and the docs. I confirmed the validator behavior with a standalone pydantic reproduction; the repo's hosted-API test fixture could not start in this sandbox, so I could not run the affected pytest cases end-to-end.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The validator blocks all proactive-trigger actions (critical regression, reproduced), and the fail() path regresses `action.triggered` links relative to base and against the PR's own test. The resolve-action linking is also wrong and the proactive/failure tests are weakened by tautological assertions. These need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
Today, `triggers.act()` in `src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py` publishes the state-change events (`prefect.automation.triggered` / `.resolved`) and then builds one `TriggeredAction` per action, which is published to the actions service. The actions service calls `Action.succeed()` or `Action.fail()` in `src/prefect/server/events/actions.py`, which emit `prefect.automation.action.triggered` plus `.executed` or `.failed`, with related resources drawn from the triggering event.

The PR threads the state-change event ID through `TriggeredAction.automation_triggered_event_id` (schema in `src/prefect/server/events/schemas/automations.py`) and emits it as an `automation-triggered-event` related resource. It also makes `triggering-event` appear on `executed` events and tidies the duplicated resource construction in `succeed()`. The new validator ties the new field to `triggering_event`, which is where the proactive-trigger regression comes from.
steps: Entry point: a trigger fires and `triggers.act(firing)` in `src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py` builds the state-change events and publishes them.

The PR picks one primary state-change event ID (Triggered preferred over Resolved) and attaches it to every `TriggeredAction` created from `source_actions`. Resolve-only actions also receive it, which is where the linking goes wrong.
`TriggeredAction` in `schemas/automations.py` gains `automation_triggered_event_id`. Its `field_validator` rejects the value when `triggering_event` is None, which is exactly the proactive case.

The actions service calls `Action.fail()` or `Action.succeed()` in `actions.py`. `succeed()` now builds one `related_resources` list (automation-triggered + triggering-event) and uses it for both `action.triggered` and `action.executed`. `fail()` swaps the lists, so `action.triggered` drops the links.
Consumers of `prefect.automation.action.*` see new `related` entries. The test files under `tests/events/server/actions/` are updated to expect the extra `triggering-event` entry on executed events.

findings.title: Proactive-trigger actions crash: new validator rejects automation_triggered_event_id when triggering_event is None
findings.body:
`act()` sets `automation_triggered_event_id` whenever a Triggered or Resolved state-change event exists. Proactive triggers fire without a triggering event (`triggering_event=None`), so the new `field_validator` raises a `ValidationError` while `TriggeredAction` is being constructed. `act()` dies before publishing, so no actions run for any proactive automation, even though the `automation.triggered` event was already published.

I reproduced the validator behavior with a standalone pydantic model using the same `info.data.get("triggering_event")` check: constructing it with `triggering_event=None` and a non-None ID raises a ValidationError. The PR's own `test_acting_publishes_an_action_message_from_a_proactive_trigger` hits this path, so it should fail as written.

The validator is also the wrong constraint. The field's purpose is linking to the state-change event, which exists for proactive triggers too. Its correctness depends on `triggering_event` being declared earlier in the model, which makes it fragile.

::diff{file="src/prefect/server/events/schemas/automations.py" lines="763-781"}

::callout{type="warning"}
This is a regression for every proactive automation, not just an edge case. Fix it before anything else.

::
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/schemas/automations.py`, the `field_validator` `validate_automation_triggered_event_id` on `TriggeredAction` (around lines 772-780) rejects a non-None `automation_triggered_event_id` when `triggering_event` is None. `act()` in `src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py` always sets this ID for Triggered/Resolved state changes, including proactive triggers that have no triggering event, so proactive automations currently raise a ValidationError and no actions are published. Remove this validator. The field is meant to link to the state-change event, which exists regardless of `triggering_event`. Then confirm `test_acting_publishes_an_action_message_from_a_proactive_trigger` in `tests/events/server/triggers/test_service.py` passes. Keep the field description as is.

findings.title: fail() swaps related lists, so action.triggered loses its links on the failure path
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/actions.py`, `Action.fail()` emits `prefect.automation.action.triggered` with `related=self._resulting_related_resources` (around line 202) and `prefect.automation.action.failed` with `related=related_resources` (around line 213). This is reversed from `Action.succeed()` and from the base commit. Change the `action.triggered` emit in `fail()` to use `related_resources`, so it carries the triggering-event and automation-triggered-event links. Keep `action.failed` on `related_resources`. Then run `test_failure_events_include_automation_triggered_event_link` in `tests/events/server/actions/test_actions_service.py`, which asserts the link on the triggered event.

findings.title: Resolve-only actions are linked to the Triggered event, not the Resolved event that prompted them
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py` `act()`, every `TriggeredAction` currently receives `primary_state_change_event_id` (around lines 445-470), which prefers Triggered over Resolved. Actions from `automation.actions_on_resolve` therefore link `automation-triggered-event` to the Triggered event even though their `triggering_event` is the Resolved event. Change the source-action tuples so each group passes the ID of its own state-change event: Triggered for `actions` and `actions_on_trigger`, Resolved for `actions_on_resolve`. Keep `automation_triggered_event_id` optional and None when that event is absent. Add a test for a firing with both Triggered and Resolved states that asserts the resolve action's link points to the Resolved event ID.

findings.title: Tautological assertions: automation_triggered_event_id is compared to itself in the trigger service tests
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/events/server/triggers/test_service.py`, both `test_acting_publishes_an_action_message_from_a_reactive_event` (around line 60) and `test_acting_publishes_an_action_message_from_a_proactive_trigger` (around line 94) pass `automation_triggered_event_id=parsed.automation_triggered_event_id` into the expected `TriggeredAction`. That compares the parsed value against itself and never checks the field. Replace it with an explicit assertion. In the reactive test, assert the ID equals the Triggered state-change event's ID that `act()` created, or at least that it is not None. Also assert the value directly on `parsed` so the test fails if the link is missing or wrong.

findings.title: Adding triggering-event to executed events is an intentional, consistently applied behavior change
findings.body:
`Action.succeed()` now builds one `related_resources` list (automation-triggered-event plus triggering-event) and uses it for both `action.triggered` and `action.executed`. Previously `executed` carried only the action's own resulting related resources. The action-specific test files (`test_pausing_resuming_*`, `test_running_deployment`, `test_sending_notification`, and others) were updated mechanically to expect the new entry. This makes `executed` consistent with `failed`, which already carried the triggering-event link.

It is a visible change for consumers that count or filter `related` on executed events, so mention it in the release notes.

findings.title: Shared primary-event computation and the resource dedupe in succeed() are clean
findings.body:
`act()` computes the primary state-change event ID once and threads it through the tuples, which keeps the three source-action comprehensions short. The `succeed()` refactor replaces the duplicated inline `Resource(...)` construction in the `action.triggered` and `action.executed` emits with the shared `resource` variable, which makes the two emits consistent.

The docs table in `docs/v3/concepts/automations.mdx` matches the event names and role names the code emits, so the reference is accurate for the success path.
